title: Defining Pydantic Models
description: Create models to structure request bodies and responses.

slides.title: Model Fields
slides.content:
# Fields with Types

A Pydantic model is a class that inherits from `BaseModel`. Each attribute is defined with a type hint.

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel

class Item(BaseModel):
    name: str
    description: str = None   # optional with default
    price: float
    tax: float = 0.0
```

- Required fields have no default.
- Optional fields can have a default (`None` or a value).
- Type hints can be from `typing` like `List`, `Optional`, `Union`.

slides.title: Using Optional Fields
slides.codeSnippet:
item1 = Item(name="Laptop", price=999.99)
print(item1)  # name='Laptop' description=None price=999.99 tax=0.0

item2 = Item(name="Phone", description="Smart", price=499.99, tax=20.0)
print(item2)  # name='Phone' description='Smart' price=499.99 tax=20.0

quizData.question: In a Pydantic model, a field without a default value is:
quizData.explanation: Fields without defaults are required when instantiating the model.

slides.title: Nested Models
slides.content:
# Composing Models

Models can contain other models, creating complex structures.

```python
class Address(BaseModel):
    street: str
    city: str

class User(BaseModel):
    name: str
    address: Address
```

- You can nest models arbitrarily.
- This is powerful for APIs with hierarchical data.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content: Use `from pydantic import BaseModel` and define models in a separate `schemas.py` file to keep your code organized.
